q: NABARD was set up on which date?
explain: NABARD began working on 12 July 1982 to implement the NABARD Act, 1981. SIDBI is the one that began on 2 April 1990.

q: NABARD was established on the recommendations of which committee?
explain: The Shivaraman Committee reviewed institutional credit arrangements for agriculture and rural development and led to NABARD.

q: Where is the headquarters of NABARD?
explain: NABARD is headquartered in Mumbai. Lucknow is the HQ of SIDBI and New Delhi that of NHB.

q: Which set of bodies did NABARD replace?
options: The Industrial Finance Corporation and the Unit Trust of India
Regional Rural Banks and Land Development Banks
The RBI’s Agricultural Credit Department and Rural Planning and Credit Cell, and the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation
The Imperial Bank and the State Financial Corporations
explain: NABARD took over the RBI’s ACD and RPCC and the ARDC, bringing rural credit functions under one apex bank.

q: As on 31 March 2013, what share of NABARD’s paid-up capital of ₹4,000 crore was held by the Government of India?
explain: The Government held ₹3,980 crore (99.50%) and the RBI ₹20 crore (0.50%) of the capital at that time.

q: What was the initial capital of NABARD?
explain: NABARD started with ₹100 crore; the paid-up capital grew to ₹4,000 crore by March 2013 and ₹4,700 crore by March 2014.

q: NABARD established JLG to tap the productive capacity of the rural population. What does JLG stand for?
explain: In a Joint Liability Group members jointly guarantee each other’s loans, which helps small rural borrowers get credit.

q: Which of these is NOT among the rural initiatives NABARD has taken up through its social work?
options: Watershed approach to soil and water conservation
explain: Currency issue is the RBI’s job. NABARD’s CSR work includes SHG linkage, watershed projects, tribal livelihoods and farmer clubs.

q: Which role best describes NABARD’s main support to rural lenders?
options: Refinancing the institutions that lend to the rural sector
Issuing export credit to large exporters
explain: NABARD is an apex agency that refinances the institutions giving investment and production credit in rural areas.

q: The apex body that deals with refinance for agriculture and rural development in India is
explain: NABARD is the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development. SIDBI serves MSMEs and IDBI industry.

q: Approximately how many partner organisations has NABARD worked with in its social innovation efforts?
explain: The study material says NABARD has partnered with about 4,000 organisations on initiatives such as SHG-bank linkage and watershed projects.

q: Which was the first Development Financial Institution set up by the Government of India after independence?
explain: IFCI (1948) was the first DFI after independence, to meet the long-term financial needs of industry.

q: In which year was IFCI reconstituted as a company to give it more operational flexibility?
explain: In 1993 IFCI became a company and was allowed to approach the capital markets directly.

q: The Industrial Finance Corporation of India provides loans to
options: Joint stock companies and cooperative societies engaged in manufacturing and processing of goods
Only government companies in the core sector
Only newly set up units in backward districts
Private limited companies and partnership firms
explain: IFCI lends only to public limited (joint stock) companies and cooperatives, not to private limited companies or partnership firms.

q: IDBI was established in 1964 by
options: A Companies Act registration by private owners
explain: IDBI was created by an Act of Parliament to provide credit and facilities for the development of Indian industry.

q: Where is IDBI’s overseas branch located?
explain: IDBI’s one overseas branch is at Dubai; its overseas centres are in Singapore and Beijing.

q: How is IDBI described in the current study material?
options: A universal bank on a core banking platform
explain: IDBI has moved from a pure development bank to a universal bank offering retail and corporate banking.

q: SIDBI was initially incorporated as a wholly owned subsidiary of which institution?
explain: SIDBI began on 2 April 1990 as a subsidiary of IDBI; ownership is now with 33 government-owned or controlled institutions.

q: Where is the headquarters of SIDBI?
explain: SIDBI is headquartered in Lucknow.

q: Which is the principal institution for promotion, financing and development of the small-scale and MSME sector?
explain: SIDBI is the principal financial institution for the MSME sector and coordinates similar institutions.

q: SIDBI’s Micro Finance branches are aimed at giving loans up to
explain: SIDBI opened seven Micro Finance branches especially for loans up to ₹5 lakh.

q: Which scheme did SIDBI introduce in 1992-93 to give direct finance to well-run small units for technology up-gradation?
explain: The equipment finance scheme gave direct finance to well-run units upgrading technology. The others came decades later.

q: What was the initial corpus of the SIDBI venture capital fund meant exclusively for small-scale units?
explain: The venture capital fund launched in the early 1990s had an initial corpus of ₹10 crore.

q: In which year was the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) set up as a SIDBI milestone?
explain: CGTMSE came in 2000, after SIDBI Venture Capital Limited (1999) and before SMERA Ratings (2005).

q: India SME Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd. (ISARC) was set up in which year?
explain: ISARC (2008) follows SMERA Ratings (2005) in the SIDBI milestone list.

q: Which SIDBI milestone year saw the launch of Certified Credit Counsellor (CCC)?
explain: MUDRA was 2015, TReDS 2016 and Certified Credit Counsellor 2017.

q: Which was SIDBI’s largest shareholder as on 4 May 2022?
explain: The Government of India held 20.85%, ahead of SBI, LIC and NABARD.

q: Among SIDBI’s four major shareholders listed for May 2022, which held the smallest stake?
explain: NABARD held 9.36%, below LIC (13.33%), SBI (15.65%) and the Government (20.85%).

q: SIDBI’s SPEED, launched in 2019, aims to speed credit to MSMEs for investing in
explain: SPEED stands for SIDBI Loan for Purchase of Equipment for Enterprise Development.

q: What does SMILE, launched by SIDBI in 2015, stand for?
options: SIDBI Make in India Soft Loan Fund for MSMEs
Small Industries Micro Investment and Loan Entity
Small Investor Make in India Loan Scheme
explain: SMILE provides soft loans for new manufacturing or service enterprises under the Make in India push.

q: The India Aspiration Fund (IAF) to boost the start-up ecosystem was launched under SIDBI in
explain: IAF came in 2015; the Fund of Funds followed in 2016.

q: The Women’s Livelihood Bond (Mahila Aajeevika Bond) announced in February 2019 offers what annual coupon and tenure?
explain: The World Bank, SIDBI and UN Women announced the bond with a 3% annual coupon and five-year tenure for rural women entrepreneurs.

q: Receivables Exchange of India Ltd (RXIL) was formed in February 2016 as a joint venture of SIDBI and which other body?
explain: RXIL, which runs the TReDS platform, is a joint venture of NSE and SIDBI.

q: EXIM Bank of India was set up in 1982 under which Act?
explain: EXIM Bank was created under the EXIM Bank of India Act 1981 and began operations in 1982, like NABARD.

q: Which of these is NOT a function of EXIM Bank?
options: Paying special attention to capital goods exports
explain: Rural refinance is NABARD’s role. EXIM Bank focuses on export-import finance.

q: Which institution is regarded as the premier export finance institution of India?
explain: The Export-Import Bank of India is the premier export finance institution.

q: ICICI Bank’s registered office is in which city, with its corporate headquarters in Mumbai?
explain: ICICI is registered in Vadodara (Gujarat) but its corporate headquarters is in Mumbai.

q: Which of these was an objective of ICICI?
options: To sponsor and underwrite new issues
explain: ICICI’s objectives included underwriting new issues and lending to private-sector industry; the others belong to RBI, NABARD and DICGC.

q: Which two banks were first designated as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) by the RBI in 2015?
explain: SBI and ICICI Bank were the first two D-SIBs; HDFC Bank was added later.

q: On which date was the National Housing Bank (NHB) set up?
explain: NHB was set up on 9 July 1988 under the National Housing Bank Act, 1987.

q: Where is the head office of NHB?
explain: NHB’s head office is in New Delhi.

q: Who contributed the entire paid-up capital of NHB when it was set up?
explain: The RBI funded NHB at the start; the Finance Act 2018 later enabled transfer of the shares to the Central Government.

q: Which of these is NOT an objective of the National Housing Bank?
options: Giving refinance to housing finance institutions and scheduled banks
Providing guarantee and underwriting facilities to housing finance institutions
explain: NHB deals with housing finance; only the RBI issues currency.

q: The National Housing Bank Act under which NHB was set up was passed in which year?
explain: NHB was set up in 1988 under the National Housing Bank Act, 1987.

q: IIFCL was set up in 2006 to give long-term finance to
explain: India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd is a wholly government-owned company for long-term infrastructure finance.

q: As on 31 March 2017, what were the authorised and paid-up capital of IIFCL?
explain: IIFCL’s authorised capital was ₹6,000 crore and paid-up capital ₹4,002 crore.

q: In 2016 the Irrigation and Water Resources Finance Corporation (IWRFC) was amalgamated with
explain: IWRFC, formed on 29 March 2008 for irrigation investment, merged into IIFCL in 2016.

q: Which sector is eligible for financial assistance from IIFCL?
explain: IIFCL supports transportation, energy, water, sanitation, communication and social and commercial infrastructure.

q: The Unit Trust of India was first set up in which year?
explain: The UTI Act was passed on 30 December 1963 and UTI was first set up on 1 February 1964.

q: UTI Bank changed its name to which bank in 2007?
explain: UTI Bank became Axis Bank in 2007.

q: Where was the headquarters of the Industrial Investment Bank of India (IIBI)?
explain: IIBI, a 100% government-owned institution, was headquartered in Kolkata and closed in 2012.

q: In which year did the Government close down the Industrial Investment Bank of India?
explain: IIBI began in 1971 as IRCL, became IRBI in 1985 and was closed in 2012.

q: The Board for Financial Supervision constituted by the RBI in 1994 undertakes consolidated supervision of which entities?
options: Commercial banks, financial institutions and NBFCs together
explain: The BFS looks at commercial banks, financial institutions and non-banking finance companies together.

q: Mutual funds fall within the supervisory purview of
explain: SEBI regulates mutual funds; IRDAI regulates insurance.

q: India’s first small finance bank was opened in which city?
explain: Capital Small Finance Bank in Jalandhar was the first, among 10 entities given in-principle approval by the RBI.

q: The Serum Institute of India, the world’s largest vaccine maker by doses, is located in
explain: Serum Institute of India is based in Pune.

q: SEBI raised the penalty on rating agencies ICRA, CARE and India Ratings to ₹1 crore each for lapses in rating NCDs of which company?
explain: IL&FS is a systemically important non-deposit-accepting core investment company registered with the RBI.

q: ICAO is a specialised agency of which body?
explain: The International Civil Aviation Organization is a UN agency that helps 193 countries cooperate in the skies.
